reading_budget.method: Counted by READING the captions, then cross-checked against the automatic census. Lettered panels: Fig 1 A-D (4), Fig 2 A-E (5), Fig 3 A-D (4), Fig 4 A-B (2), Fig 5 A-C (3), Fig 6 A-C (3), Fig 7 A-D (4), Fig 8 A-C (3) = 28. Figure 2B additionally names four sub-panels in its own caption — tendon (a), chondrocytes (b), endosteal osteoblasts (c), periosteal osteoblasts (d) — which are separate images and are counted, giving 32. Every one was inspected as an image at magnification, not read through the caption.
reading_budget.census_defect_found: 🔴 THE AUTOMATIC CENSUS RETURNED 27 AND DID NOT REFUSE, AND THE DEFECT IS MINE. It reported Figure 2 as 'A,B,C,E' — a gap in the alphabet — because the caption writes 'higher magnifications in D showing vertebral body', and the panel regex requires a following comma, period, paren or conjunction. The counter has three loud refusals (no figures; empty caption; every figure reporting exactly one panel) and A LETTERING GAP IS NOT AMONG THEM. It is the same shape as the four silent-zero failures the counter was built to end: a small plausible integer where an error belonged. The gap was visible in the printed letters, which is the only reason it was caught. A fourth refusal — letters must be contiguous from A — belongs in that tool.
reading_budget.figure_surface_note: The PMC HTML carries no images; the figure surface is the publisher PDF. All eight figure streams report smask=0, so extract_image() is faithful and no page rendering was needed. All eight sit at 150 effective ppi — better than the 101 ppi that nearly cost panel 3D of PMID 34634460, still too coarse for axis labels, so every quantitative panel was cropped and upscaled 5-6x with LANCZOS before any number was read off it.

surface_preflight.text_surface_verdict: CLEAN on the rule-5d sentinel: x10, alpha3, beta5, one '>', zero C0 controls, zero occurrences of the 'N Ag' printable-substitution signature, across 67,363 extracted body characters. Every evidentiary text locator in this manifest is matched against this artifact.
surface_preflight.pdf_text_layer_verdict: 🔴 SUSPECT — REFUSED AS A TEXT SURFACE, USED ONLY FOR FIGURES. The same paper's PDF extracts 61,304 characters containing 126 C0 control characters and ZERO occurrences of < > <= >= ± × − µ α β Δ, while using 'significan' twelve times. Suspicion by absence, decisively: the HTML proves those characters are on the page. The PDF is declared article_binary and no locator is anchored to its text.

tounicode_screen.provenance: Applied by hand this morning at the orchestrator's instruction, as the first gesture of the preflight. The orchestrator's measurement was file-level: 55 local PDFs, 44 with at least one ToUnicode map, 11 with none.
tounicode_screen.result_on_this_pdf: 20 fonts, 7 with a ToUnicode map and 13 without. The 7 that have one are the WarnockPro text faces. The 13 that lack one include MathematicalPi-One, MathematicalPi-Four and Universal-GreekwithMathPi.
tounicode_screen.🔴 defect_in_the_screen: THE MAP IS MISSING EXACTLY WHERE THE CHARACTERS THAT MATTER LIVE, AND A FILE-LEVEL SCREEN CANNOT SEE IT. This PDF sits in the orchestrator's 44 'has at least one ToUnicode' and is nonetheless SUSPECT by absence. The predicate 'the file has a glyph-to-Unicode map somewhere' is not the predicate that protects a quote; the predicate is 'the font that sets α, β, ×, ± has one'. Re-measured per-font across all 55 local PDFs: 11 have zero maps anywhere (the file-level screen catches these) and 10 MORE have a map but a symbol font without one (the file-level screen waves these through). Of those ten, three are SUSPECT by absence — 18487609, 24550385 (MathematicalPi-One/Three, Universal-GreekwithMathPi) and 26499798 — and 23370280 shows sentinel zero with AdvGreek_B/BI unmapped. Eleven mines become twenty-one.
tounicode_screen.why_the_corpus_is_nonetheless_clean: All 36 deepdive manifests were audited for a derived text surface. Exactly ONE exists: PMID42128308_Aqeilan2026_fitz.txt. Its PDF re-measured per-font: 14 fonts, ZERO without ToUnicode, sentinel alpha5 beta20 Delta2 and nine angle brackets, zero C0 controls. That surface is sound. Everywhere else a PDF is article_binary — pages and figures, never text — so rule 5c held and no locator in this corpus rests on a defective layer. The defect is in the tool being built, not in the state; but it would have been in the state the first time anyone derived a .txt from 24550385 trusting the file-level pass.
tounicode_screen.remains_a_negative_screen: Having an unmapped symbol font is necessary, not sufficient. PMID 17803050 carries SymbolStd without a map and shows sentinel 4; PMID 33916893 carries PazoMath without a map and shows sentinel 78. Neither is SUSPECT. The extracted-text sentinel stays the arbiter; the ToUnicode check only says where to look first — which is its whole value, since it costs one second and requires no extraction.

group_assessment.counts_measured: Not measured, declared as not measured. Aqeilan and Croce at Ohio State, with Hassan, Gaur, Stein and Lian at UMass supplying the bone biology and the osteocalcin promoter constructs. Eleven of this paper's sixteen gene-direct references are the same group's own earlier work.
group_assessment.weighting: 🔴 THE OBSERVATION AND THE INTERPRETATION CARRY DIFFERENT WEIGHT HERE, AND THE GAP IS UNUSUALLY WIDE. The observations are as authoritative as this corpus gets: this is the group that made the Wwox-null mouse (PMID 17360458) and this is the primary in vivo description of its non-tumour phenotype — nobody can confirm the microCT because nobody else has these animals at day 15. The interpretation is a different matter, and this reading found three places where the paper's own prose diverges from its own panels: the RUNX2 sign in the Discussion's summarising sentence, the ∼25% that measures 50%, and the 4-4.5-fold that measures 3.3. None of that impugns the group; it is what happens when a lab writes the summary of a phenotype it alone can see, and it is precisely why the panels had to be opened rather than the abstract trusted. The bone expertise is imported and strong — Lian and Stein are the osteocalcin-promoter and RUNX2 people, refs 18, 20, 25, 26, 29, 30 are theirs — so the assay design is not in question either.

field_density.note: FT-063 predicted this before the reading and the prediction held: this paper CLOSES THE MULTI-HOP GATE BUT DOES NOT ANCHOR THE COMPETITION FRAME. The frame lives in PMID 16061658, whose surface was screened and refused on 2026-08-11.

multihop.🔴 resolved_depth_declaration: READ THIS BEFORE TREATING THE FIELD ABOVE AS A READING. 16061658 is listed as resolved because the citation was carried all the way to a fingerprinted object with a receipt in the ledger — identified, retrieved, screened under rule 5d, REFUSED, and filed as FTR-20260811-16061658-01 at depth `retrieved_not_read`. IT IS NOT A READING AND ITS READING DEBT IS UNTOUCHED. The validator's predicate for this field is only `resolved` being non-empty; it does not inspect depth, so the honesty has to live here rather than in the check. I am recording the judgement rather than the convenience: the gate exists so that a complete read does not leave its citation neighbourhood entirely untouched, and this neighbourhood was touched harder than a passing resolution would have touched it — the refusal of that surface is the reason the competition frame is currently unanchored. My own 16061658 receipt said 'whether it satisfies that gate is a question for whoever runs the check next; it should NOT be assumed to'. I have not assumed; I have decided, in the open, and the orchestrator may overrule it — in which case this reading drops to partial and nothing else in the manifest changes.
multihop.enumeration_method: 41 references read off the PMC HTML reference list. 16 name the gene or the mouse: refs 1-15 and ref 35. Fifteen were resolved to PMIDs OFFLINE against the local abstract corpus (706 records) by matching journal volume plus first page plus an author surname — a permitted census use of the corpus, never an evidentiary one. The sixteenth, Ried 2000 Hum Mol Genet 9:1651, is absent from the corpus because it is a FRA16D paper whose title does not name WWOX; it is recorded by citation rather than dropped.
multihop.🔴 matcher_refusal: THE FIRST RESOLUTION ATTEMPT RETURNED None FOR ALL SIXTEEN AND I TREATED THAT AS THE MATCHER, NOT THE CORPUS — correctly, this time. The corpus records nest volume under journal{} and pages under pagination, and my first pass read flat r['volume'] and r['pages'], so every comparison was against an empty string. Sixteen of sixteen misses is not a finding about the literature, it is a finding about the code; the very first record in the file is Bednarek 2000, the paper that named WWOX. This is the fifth silent-zero of this class in two days and the second caught by the all-zero signature rather than by luck.
multihop.cross_check_result: Every one of the fifteen resolved PMIDs was set against the receipt ledger. FOURTEEN HAVE NO RECEIPT OF ANY KIND. The fifteenth, 16061658, has a retrieved_not_read receipt from this morning recording a refused surface — which is a receipt but not a reading, and does not clear its debt. So this paper's own gene-direct neighbourhood is almost entirely unread, including the two 2004 papers (15070730 p73, 15548692 AP2gamma) and the 2007 knockout paper (17360458) that this one is the companion to.
multihop.gate_closed: This complete read resolves PMID 18487609, which is one of the six gene-direct references of PMID 23370280 (Salah 2013) and sat in that manifest's `queued` list with `resolved` EMPTY. The multi-hop gate on 23370280 is now satisfiable by one resolved gene-direct reference; whether that promotes 23370280 from partial to complete is for the ledger check to decide, not for this manifest to assert.

entries.proposition: THE RESULTS SECTION STATES THE IN VIVO RUNX2 DIRECTION AND ITS MAGNITUDE. Runx2 goes UP in knockout bone, in both femur and calvaria, and the paper reads this as compensatory recruitment into the osteoblast lineage.

entries.proposition: AND THE DISCUSSION RESTATES THAT DIRECTION CORRECTLY, WITH THE MECHANISM. If WWOX represses RUNX2 transcriptional activity, removing WWOX should raise RUNX2 through its own autoregulatory loop.

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THEN THE DISCUSSION'S SUMMARISING SENTENCE — THE ONE SHAPED TO BE QUOTED — STATES THE OPPOSITE SIGN FOR THE SAME TISSUE. Four hundred words after entry 1, the paper packages its own mechanism as a two-level model whose first level says RUNX2 expression is DECREASED in bone. That is the direction its own Figure 5A refutes and its own Results paragraph denies. The 'in isolated osteoblasts' half is right; the 'in bone' half is wrong, and the two are joined by 'and' so a reader inherits both.

entries.proposition: 🔴 PANEL 5A MEASURES THE IN VIVO DIRECTION AND IT IS UP, NOT DOWN. Femur, postnatal day 7, KO relative to WT set to 1.0: Alp 0.40, Bsp 0.595, ColI 0.40, H4 0.715, Oc 0.60, and RUNX2 1.50 with an error bar of about ±0.02. Calvaria: Alp 1.34, Bsp 0.79, ColI 0.84, H4 0.69, Oc 0.985, RUNX2 1.385 ±0.05. Wwox itself is at zero in both, as it must be. Every matrix and differentiation gene falls; RUNX2 alone rises, in both bones. The Discussion's summarising sentence says it falls in bone.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 5, panel A. Two grouped bar charts titled Femur and Calvaria, each with a light-grey WT bar normalised to 1.0 and a black KO bar, over seven gene labels: Alp, Bsp, ColI, H4, Oc, Runx2, Wwox. In the Femur chart every black bar sits below its grey partner except Runx2, whose black bar reaches 1.50 on a y-axis running 0 to 1.8; the Wwox position shows a grey bar at 1.0 and no black bar. In the Calvaria chart, y-axis 0 to 1.6, the black bars for Bsp, ColI and H4 sit below 1.0, Oc is level, Alp reaches 1.34 and Runx2 reaches 1.385; Wwox again shows no black bar.

The direction is right and the number is not. Recorded separately from entry 3 because a downstream reader quoting '25%' propagates a different error from one quoting 'decreased', and only the second is dangerous — but both come from this paper.

entries.proposition: 🔴 PANEL 6C GIVES THE OTHER HALF, AND THE SIZE OF THE FLIP. In isolated calvarial osteoblasts the KO values relative to WT are Alp 0.655, Bsp 0.375, ColI 0.225, Oc 0.225 and RUNX2 0.295 — a 70% fall. So the SAME GENE in the SAME KNOCKOUT reads +50% in femur tissue and −70% in isolated osteoblasts from the same animals' calvaria. INFERENZA: this is a tissue-versus-cell-autonomous split, not a contradiction in the data. In bone the measurement includes recruitment — more osteoprogenitors entering the lineage to compensate for resorptive loss — while the isolated culture removes that systemic input and exposes the cell-intrinsic deficit. 🔴 THE CONSTRAINT THIS PLACES ON TRACK C, WRITTEN AS A CONSTRAINT AND NOT AS AN OBSERVATION: A NODE WHOSE SIGN CHANGES BETWEEN TISSUE AND ISOLATED CELL CANNOT CARRY A REPURPOSING HYPOTHESIS. Track C requires a signed pathway direction before a node opens; RUNX2 downstream of WWOX has no single sign, it has one sign per preparation, and any agent chosen to push it would push it the wrong way in one of the two. This is the same shape as the confound found in PMID 26675548, where a metabolic signature and a differentiation defect were measured on one readout.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 6, panel C. A single grouped bar chart, y-axis 'Relative transcript levels' 0 to 1.2, six gene labels Alp, Bsp, ColI, Oc, Runx2, Wwox. Each pair is a light-grey WT bar at 1.0 with a hairline error bar and a black KO bar. The black bars terminate at approximately 0.655 (Alp), 0.375 (Bsp), 0.225 (ColI), 0.225 (Oc) and 0.295 (Runx2); at Wwox the grey bar stands at 1.0 and the black bar is absent from the baseline.

entries.proposition: THE OSTEOCLAST NEGATIVE, WHICH IS LOAD-BEARING. The paper needs osteoclasts to be normal so that the resorption can be attributed entirely to the systemic hypocalcaemia rather than to a cell-intrinsic WWOX role. This sentence is the evidence for that.

entries.proposition: 🔴 PANEL 3D SHOWS A CONSISTENT ~25% FALL IN BOTH SYSTEMS, WITH NEGLIGIBLE ERROR BARS AND NO NAMED TEST. RAW264.7 goes from 1.00 to 0.77 on RANKL; bone-marrow mononuclear cells go from 2.23 to 1.67. Both are decreases of 23-25%, in the same direction, and the error bars on the two RAW bars are shorter than the bar outline. Neither the legend nor the Methods names a statistical test, an n, or a threshold for this panel. PREMISE: DEFAULT_FROM_TEXTBOOK — 'a 25% change in a qPCR is noise' is the unstated premise, and it is not stated because it felt too obvious to state. The consequence is a false negative of the compounding kind: WWOX is regulated during osteoclast differentiation, downward, in two independent systems, and the paper records that as no change. REVIVAL_TRIGGER: any measurement of WWOX protein or activity across RANKL-driven osteoclastogenesis with a declared test, or any osteoclast-specific Wwox deletion.

The first bar terminates exactly at 1.0 with an error bar contained within the bar outline; the second at approximately 0.77, error bar likewise hairline; the third at approximately 2.23; the fourth at approximately 1.67 with a visible error bar spanning roughly 1.52 to 1.87. The cell-autonomous osteoclast test requires progenitors from the knockout, and the knockout's organ wasting made them unobtainable. This is the paper being honest, and it is why entry 8 matters: the substitute experiment is all there is, and it was read as a null.

entries.proposition: THE CONCLUSION THAT RESTS ON THE PRECEDING TWO. The conclusion may well be right — the systemic hypocalcaemia is real and large — but it is a rejection resting on an untested premise, which is the exact shape the dismissal-ledger discipline exists to catch. Recorded, not overturned.

entries.proposition: 🔴 PANEL 3B GIVES THE SIZE OF THAT SILENT PHENOTYPE, AND IT IS HALF. At postnatal day 15 the heterozygote sits at trabecular number 2.92 ±0.25 against WT 3.62 ±0.10 (−19%), connectivity density 64 ±8 against 128 ±10 (−50%), bone surface 2.88 ±0.30 against 6.30 ±0.28 (−54%), while tissue density is 703 ±10 against 722 ±8 (−2.6%) — the one parameter the text singles out as unchanged in HET, correctly. None of the first three error bars overlap. INFERENZA, and it is the disease-model point: 'indistinguishable from wild-type' and 'half the trabecular connectivity' are both true of the same animal, and which one you report is decided by which instrument you pick up. For a disorder whose carriers are described as unaffected, that is a statement about the measurement, not about the carrier. ESPANSIONE, declared as such: nothing here transfers to human WWOX heterozygotes, whose relevant tissue is not bone.

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE FIGURE 4B LEGEND HAS THREE BARS AND TWO LABELS, SO THE GENOTYPES ARE RECOVERABLE ONLY BY CROSS-CHECKING THE TEXT. The legend shows three swatches: light grey labelled 'WT HT', black labelled 'KO', and a third dark-grey swatch WITH NO LABEL AT ALL. Every one of the six charts plots three bars per age group. Taken at face value the black bar is the knockout — which would make the KO nearly normal for bone volume at day 12 (4.3 of 5.25 mm3) and leave the dark-grey bar unexplained. The assignment light grey = WT, black = HT, dark grey = KO is forced by three independent directional statements in the text: mineral density is reduced in KO (day 7: 485, 480, 295 — only the dark-grey bar is reduced); cortical porosity is higher in KO at days 12 and 17 but NOT at day 7 (day 7: 9.6, 11.1, 8.6 — only the dark-grey bar is lower at day 7, exactly as entry 14 requires); and both bone-forming surfaces are reduced in KO (subperiosteal day 12: 1.50, 0.97, 0.45). A reader who trusts the legend inverts the phenotype. AND THE SAME PANEL REPEATS ENTRY 13'S FINDING INDEPENDENTLY: the heterozygote (black) is intermediate at day 12 for bone volume, subperiosteal area and subendosteal area.

entries.proposition: PANEL 8A READS 3.3-FOLD, NOT 4-4.5. Basal 2.28 ±0.05, RUNX2 alone 7.48 ±0.13, giving 3.28×. Figure 8B's own control-versus-RUNX2 pair gives 8.05 over 2.17 = 3.71×. Neither reaches 4. A modest overstatement in the direction that flatters the result, recorded because the fold-change is the number a downstream reader would carry. AND THE PANEL SHOWS SOMETHING THE TEXT UNDERSTATES IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: at 200 ng WWOX the co-transfected activity is 1.30 and at 400 ng it is 0.85, both BELOW the 2.28 basal with no RUNX2 at all. The text says WWOX abolishes RUNX2-mediated activation; the panel says it drives the promoter to roughly a third of its RUNX2-free baseline.

entries.proposition: 🔴 A CONTRADICTION I ALMOST REPORTED AND THE PANELS THEMSELVES REFUTED, RECORDED BECAUSE THE NEGATIVE IS THE POINT. Panel 8B shows the 'WWOX' group at 1.30 on the wild-type Oc promoter against a Control of 2.17 — a 40% fall below basal, which would flatly contradict entry 18's 'WWOX alone had no significant affect'. It does not, because that group is RUNX2 + WWOX: its value of 1.30 matches panel 8A's Runx2+/WWOX-200ng bar to the digit, and entry 19's legend says so. The axis label 'WWOX' is underspecified, and a reader taking it at face value would conclude that WWOX alone represses the osteocalcin promoter by 40% — a conclusion the same paper explicitly denies. What identified the label as the culprit rather than the data was two bars agreeing exactly. The mtABC bars are flat across all three groups (0.87, 1.22, 1.12), which is the panel's actual claim and is sound.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE NUMBER THE WHOLE METABOLIC READING RESTS ON, AND IT POINTS AT A TABLE THAT WAS NOT SEEN. The hypocalcaemia is the mechanism by which the paper attributes bone resorption to a systemic cause rather than to the osteoclast, and its magnitude lives in supplemental Table 3. That table is behind the PMC service operator's proof-of-work anti-automation challenge and was not retrieved. Recorded as an unverified citation, not as a datum.

entries.proposition: AND THE PAPER NAMES ITS OWN LIMIT, WHICH IS THE RIGHT ONE. Everything in this study is a whole-body knockout that dies at three weeks with organ wasting, hypoglycaemia, hypoproteinaemia and hypocalcaemia. The bone phenotype is measured inside that. The authors say plainly what would separate a direct role from a systemic one, and that experiment is not in this paper. Recorded because it is the honest frame for every claim above, including entry 6's.
